Ray Gun no. 12, “The LA episode”

A Ray Gun issue from the turn of 1993–94, with Deborah Harry interviewing L7 on the cover and headlines inside that are scattered, doubled, blurred, and sprayed.

Source
Display Graphic Design Collection: Ray Gun, No. 12
Creator
David Carson
Made
December 1993/January 1994 (Wikipedia); Display gives “December/January 1993”
Style
Grunge typography (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Raw, chaotic, dirty
Evidence
Inspected five photographs (1600 × 1279 each) of one copy offered by Display in scratchpad copies: the cover and four interior spreads. The copy has no collection number. Not stored.
Reviewed
28 September 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

Display lists the issue as no. 12, 10 × 12 inches, 108 pages, art direction by David Carson, with L7 interviewed by Deborah Harry, and features on Mazzy Star, Redd Kross, Moby, and Yo La Tengo. Display.

Wikipedia’s issue list dates no. 12 to December 1993/January 1994, with L7 on the cover. Wikipedia).

Observed

  • The cover is a full-bleed colour photograph of L7 with a bright green masthead bar reading “R AYGUN,” in heavy black sans-serif with an odd gap and a trailing comma.
  • Cover lines are a condensed sans-serif in white capitals, right-aligned in a narrow column.
  • The Bad Religion spread scatters large serif capitals, some in outline, across a brown duotone band photograph and over the body text; a brown splash surrounds one letter.
  • Pull-quote lines are set in several sizes and faces and overlap the text columns.
  • The Mazzy Star headline is blurred, doubled, and scratched, repeated across both pages, with yellow spray-paint marks over the body text.
  • The Mazzy Star body text is an italic serif set in a tilted, bending column; the photograph has a rough black border.
  • The Redd Kross opener uses a spiky decorative serif for the headline and byline over a red duotone photograph of sneakers.

Why it belongs

This issue shows how grunge damage is concentrated in headlines and ornaments. Body text stays set in conventional serifs and a typewriter face, even when it is tilted or overlapped.

Borrow

Repeat a headline twice with a slight offset and blur, as a misregistered print.

Scatter the letters of one heading across a spread in mixed outline and solid capitals.

Add one spray or stain mark in a muted accent colour over body text, not over the headline.
